Connor —

Thanks for the quick intro call today. As we move through FinSecure's vendor review, the security team has a short list of technical artifacts we need about abuse prevention and misuse monitoring to close our evaluation. Can you provide the following items by EOD Wednesday (2026-03-10)?

1) Summary of automated misuse detection signals you surface (policy categories, heuristics, ML models, and observable indicators)
2) Alerting & triage workflow: how alerts are generated, enrichment, severity levels, and human review SLAs
3) Data retention and audit logging for inference requests and telemetry (retention windows, indices, redaction policy)
4) Integration patterns for SIEM/SOAR (example alert schema, supported transports — syslog, Kafka, HTTP)
5) Evidence: SOC 2 report or equivalent, and a recent pen-test summary if available
6) Any configurable controls for customers to tune detection thresholds, blocklists, or content filters

If you can send a short technical appendix and an example alert JSON for our security engineers, that would be most helpful. We're tight on schedule — appreciate anything you can share.

-Lena

Hi Lena —

Thanks, great to meet earlier. Please find inline answers + attached appendix (redwood-abuse-detection-appendix.pdf) and a compact alert-schema example (alert-schema-stub.json). High level answers below; the appendix has diagrams and sample telemetry extracts.

1) Detection signals
- Policy categories: fraud/financial-misuse, PII exfiltration, hate/harassment, self-harm, copyright infringement.
- Signal types: model-output classifiers (multi-label), heuristic rules (regex, token-based scoring), anomaly detectors on request patterns (bursting, unusual prompt templates), and user-behavior heuristics (IP/geolocation velocity).
- Models: ensemble of lightweight classifiers run server-side (logits + calibrated confidence). We log model scores and rule triggers for audit.

2) Alerting & triage
- Alerts are generated when a rule or model crosses a customer-configurable threshold. Each alert includes: severity (info/warn/critical), derived policy tag, evidence excerpt (redacted), and related request IDs.
- Enrichment: automated enrichment pulls recent session history, top-k cache hits, and associated metadata (region, model version, token counts).
- Human review: customers can route alerts to Redwood's SOC (managed option) or export to their SIEM. Default human-review SLA for critical alerts in managed triage is 2 hours; for standard escalations it's 24 hours.

3) Data retention & audit logging
- Inference request logs are retained by default 90 days. Customers can configure retention to 30/90/365 days for request-level telemetry.
- Audit logs (policy changes, role access, admin actions) retained for 365 days by default; longer retention available on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Redaction: PII extraction can be automatically redacted using configurable masks before storage. Appendix includes retention config examples.

4) SIEM/SOAR integration
- Supported transports: HTTPS webhook (JSON), syslog, and Kafka (Avro/JSON).
- Example alert schema attached (alert-schema-stub.json). Fields include request_id, timestamp, severity, policy_tags, evidence_excerpt (redacted), model_version, and enrichment pointers (drive links).

5) Evidence
- SOC 2 Type II report (attached: SOC2-report-2025.pdf) and penetration test executive summary available on request.

6) Customer-configurable controls
- Threshold sliders per policy category, per-model filtering, allowlist/blocklist for prompt templates, and auto-block vs. alert-only modes.

Action items: Marissa — can you attach the SOC 2 PDF and the network-flow diagram we keep for procurement? Neha, please confirm exact retention windows we can commit to for Dedicated customers (appendix mentions 7/30/90/365 options).

Thanks — sending the appendix now. Happy to jump on a short session to walk your engineers through the schema.

Cheers,
